source.scope: Journal-fit targeting reconciled with TARGET_JOURNALS.md strategic priority ranking (2026-11-09)
source.manuscriptTitle: Measurement Validity Before Model Geometry: A Reproducible Audit of Bounded Response Models

targetJournals.name: Social Indicators Research
targetJournals.focus: Composite social indicators, cross-national measurement and quality-of-life methodology.
targetJournals.audience: Social-indicator researchers, comparative sociologists and welfare-state methodologists.
methodsExpectations: Composite indicators defended on measurement grounds, not assertion
Explicit treatment of reliability, dimensionality and construct withdrawal
Transparent statement of sample and support limits
deskRejectTriggers: Composite constructs reported without reliability evidence
Claims scaled beyond the observed country-year support
Fit statistics presented without a baseline comparison

framingAdjustments.abstract: Lead with the measurement audit and the construct withdrawals; report the linear-baseline comparison as a finding.
framingAdjustments.introduction: Position the paper as a reproducibility protocol for composite-indicator panels.
framingAdjustments.conclusion: Close on auditability and disclosed limits, not on model performance.

targetJournals.name: Technological Forecasting and Social Change
targetJournals.focus: Societal change under technological and structural transition, with computational methods.
targetJournals.audience: Interdisciplinary social-change researchers comfortable with quantitative pipelines.
methodsExpectations: Relevance of the structural drivers (urbanization, inequality, media, education) to societal change
Computational pipeline described well enough to re-execute
Explicit boundary between descriptive mapping and forecasting
deskRejectTriggers: Methods presented with no societal-change argument
Forecast language applied to a non-forecasting design

framingAdjustments.abstract: Foreground the urbanization-inequality-belief question, then the audit that constrains what can be said.
framingAdjustments.introduction: Frame the country panel as a societal-transition panel.
framingAdjustments.conclusion: State which transition claims survive the audit and which do not.

targetJournals.name: Big Data & Society
targetJournals.focus: Critical and methodological inquiry into data-driven social research and its infrastructure.
targetJournals.audience: Computational social scientists and critical data-studies scholars.
methodsExpectations: Reflexive treatment of what the data infrastructure can and cannot measure
deskRejectTriggers: Unreflexive use of survey aggregates as ground truth
No discussion of data-access and redistribution limits

framingAdjustments.abstract: Emphasise that the audit shows what the measurement infrastructure cannot support.
framingAdjustments.introduction: Situate the paper in critical data studies as well as in social-indicator methodology.
framingAdjustments.conclusion: Frame construct withdrawal as an infrastructure finding, not a modelling failure.

targetJournals.name: PLOS ONE
targetJournals.focus: Methodologically sound research judged on rigour rather than perceived impact.
targetJournals.audience: Broad multidisciplinary readership and methods reviewers.
methodsExpectations: Complete reporting of the analysis pipeline
Data availability statement consistent with the WVS licence
Reproducibility artifacts and a correction note for revised results
deskRejectTriggers: Claims unsupported by the reported evidence

framingAdjustments.abstract: Plain statement of the audit, the withdrawals, and the baseline comparison.
framingAdjustments.introduction: Keep the contribution narrow and checkable.
framingAdjustments.conclusion: Point to the replication runbook and the correction note.

targetJournals.name: Scientific Reports
targetJournals.focus: Technically valid research across the natural and social sciences.
methodsExpectations: Statistical claims proportionate to the design
Validation protocol separated from exploratory analysis
deskRejectTriggers: Validation protocol not separated from headline claims

framingAdjustments.abstract: Lead with the audit protocol and its four hard gates.
framingAdjustments.introduction: Present the bounded model as an object under test, not as a result.
framingAdjustments.conclusion: Emphasise the reusable gate set over the specific fit.

majorClaims.claim: A reproducible audit protocol enforces construct reliability, item-overlap, design rank and baseline comparison as hard release gates.

rationale.technological_forecasting_social_change: Methodology is a means; the gate set is still a transferable tool.
rationale.big_data_society: The gate set is an infrastructure critique in executable form.
rationale.plos_one: Rigour-first contribution with no impact claim required.

majorClaims.claim: Three of four candidate composites fail internal consistency on the WVS Trend File and are withdrawn rather than reported with a caveat.

rationale.social_indicators_research: Construct withdrawal is the journal's own methodological standard.
rationale.technological_forecasting_social_change: A negative measurement result may read as scope-narrowing to this audience.
rationale.big_data_society: Negative results about survey infrastructure are on-scope.
rationale.plos_one: Negative and methods results are acceptable.
rationale.scientific_reports: Validity-first framing is legible to technical reviewers.

majorClaims.claim: In the previous panel the outcome was an exact rescaling of a predictor (corr = 1.0); the rebuilt panel contains 207 complete-case country-years across 83 countries, 1990-2023.

rationale.social_indicators_research: Sample and defect disclosure are expected.
rationale.technological_forecasting_social_change: Shows the panel is a real comparative dataset.
rationale.big_data_society: Defect and correction are the paper's evidential core.
rationale.plos_one: Disclosure of changed results is required practice.

majorClaims.claim: On the surviving constructs the saturating map does not beat an ordinary linear regression on identical rows and folds.

rationale.social_indicators_research: A stated model comparison is a strength for indicator work.
rationale.technological_forecasting_social_change: A null functional-form result weakens the transition story for this venue.
rationale.big_data_society: Contesting the modelling claim is on-scope.

majorClaims.claim: Fixed-coefficient country-out validation is negative in every tier (Tier A -2.01, B -0.97, C -0.90) and is reported as such.

rationale.social_indicators_research: Disclosed negative OOS is preferable to suppressed OOS.
rationale.technological_forecasting_social_change: Predictive failure undercuts applied relevance here.
rationale.big_data_society: Failure disclosure fits the venue's critical stance.
rationale.scientific_reports: Reviewers may read negative OOS as a validity problem rather than a finding.

majorClaims.claim: Inference is conditioned on 207 unique country-years; Tier C (22 parameters, 12.85 obs/param) is exploratory and excluded from headline claims.

rationale.social_indicators_research: Thin-support macro panels are routine in this venue.
rationale.technological_forecasting_social_change: Thin support limits applied claims for a forecasting-oriented audience.
rationale.big_data_society: Support limits are a data-infrastructure argument.

majorClaims.claim: Interpretation is descriptive and non-causal; no policy-optimal recommendation is made.

rationale.technological_forecasting_social_change: Policy adjacency usually implies causal language at this venue.
rationale.big_data_society: Non-causal restraint matches the venue's epistemology.

majorClaims.claim: The contribution is an executable audit workflow plus a disclosed correction, not an empirically validated response surface.

rationale.social_indicators_research: Methodological contribution with composite indicators is on-scope.
rationale.technological_forecasting_social_change: A workflow-only contribution may be judged insufficiently applied here.
rationale.big_data_society: Workflow-as-critique is central to the venue.
rationale.scientific_reports: Reusable protocol is a legitimate contribution.

summaryByJournal.recommendedPositioning: Primary target: composite-indicator methodology with construct withdrawals and a disclosed correction.
Secondary: reframe around societal transition and keep the model claim weak.
Secondary: lead with the infrastructure critique rather than the fit.
Fallback with high acceptance odds: rigour-first, correction disclosed.
Fallback: similar to PLOS ONE, stricter on predictive claims.
